summary.text: Chaz Molder is the mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, an attorney first elected mayor in 2018 and re-elected in 2022; he announced he would not seek a third term. A University of Tennessee and University of Memphis law school graduate, he is the Democratic nominee for the open 5th District seat and is running on lowering costs, health care access and labor protections.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Tennessee; a graduate of Columbia Central High School and, in his words, a product of Columbia's public schools.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, in 2005 and a law degree from the University of Memphis Cecil C. Humphreys School of Law in 2009.
Works as an attorney, according to Ballotpedia.
Elected mayor of Columbia in 2018 with 65 percent of the vote; his campaign website says he was then the youngest mayor in Tennessee and in the city's 200-plus-year history.
Won a second term as mayor in 2022 with just under 60 percent of the vote, then announced he would not run for a third term.
According to his campaign website, as mayor he has passed eight balanced budgets with no property tax increases and says he saved taxpayers $10.5 million through fiscal management.
Formed the Columbia Mayor's Youth Council as mayor.
Won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary for the 5th District with 40.9 percent of the vote.
According to his campaign website, he is married to Elizabeth Molder, they have three children in local public schools, and the family attends First United Methodist Church in Columbia.
